reviews.title: Worst experience
reviews.text: To start with, our family has flown with more than 8 different airlines in the span of 20 years, and we have never seen anything like this before. Over the course of 2 months, we flew with SkyUp airlines three times. The first two flights were to and from Hurghada. When we boarded the plane, we were surprised by the small legroom. Even as someone who is 1.55m tall, it was difficult for me to sit through the 5-hour-long flight. The plane appeared old and was really loud. Around 1.5 hours into the flight, I woke up because my head, hands, and legs were freezing. When my father asked for a blanket, they inquired if we were cold and informed us that there were no blankets on board. Other passengers were also complaining about the cold. They increased the temperature slightly, making it a bit warmer. No food or water was offered to us, even though free water on board was advertised. On the return flight, we were more prepared and wore our coats and two pairs of socks each. Again, there was no legroom, it was cold, impossible to fall asleep due to uncomfortable seats, and no food or water provided. The third flight was from Antalya. Initially, we were told we would fly with TailWind airlines, so we were disappointed to see a SkyUp airplane. This time it was the Shakhtar model. At first, the airplane looked nice and new, but we soon realized that the seats were even more uncomfortable than the ones on the flights to and from Hurghada. reviews.title: AVOID THIS UNPROFESSIONAL, IGNORANT, TIMEWASTER AIRLINE
reviews.text: 13-09-2021 Baku-Lviv. The incompetent crew made a decision to take off in bad weather at the destination airport and were unable to land the aircraft upon arrival. As a result, we had a delay for +7 hours and a missed connection flight. The ignorant staff took no responsibility for the incident. Foreign passengers stuck at the Ukrainian airport had to reach their destination at their own expense including hotel expenses. The airline avoids refund claims by offering to send a letter to an address in Ukraine and introducing other paperwork hoping that the passengers are busy/lazy to do all this. But keep in mind that the airline is responsible in accordance with the Warsaw convention. If you had such an incident, don't hesitate to hire a lawyer and sue the airline. They will be forced to compensate all costs. SkyUp is a horrible company and ready to ruin your day for your money.
